Renormalization therefore has the effect of condensing the somewhat complicated recursions

the other hand, this conjecture is readily phrased in two halves, and Redmond was able to prove
the most important half, and his proof is included in this paper as Theorem 1. Higher order

after.text:
Our first result, the so-called 3-Conjecture, relates to the Quadratic Polynomial Riemann
hypothesis and the 4-term recursions (6). We have the following conjecture.

Conjecture 1 (3-Conjecture) The sequence of polynomials qn , n = 1, 2, . . ., as defined through
the 4-term recursion (6) have real zeros if and only if C ≥ 3. Moreover, when C ≥ 3, the zeros
of qn+1 interlace the zeros of qn .

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For a monic three-term recurrence, a unique functional makes the sequence orthogonal; positivity is equivalent to positive recurrence coefficients and Hankel determinants and implies simple real interlacing zeros. section_entries.label: Path interpretations and Hankel determinants
section_entries.mathematical_role: Uses modified sign-reversing involutions to count Hankel determinants by non-intersecting paths, proves a Catalan-Hankel evaluation, and records tableau encodings and a missing direct bijection.

unit_result_entry.title: Both path models admit tableau encodings, but their equality lacks a direct bijection
unit_result_entry.why_material: Non-intersecting Hankel paths correspond to bounded column-strict staircase tableaux, while osculating ASM paths correspond to strict Gelfand patterns or shifted ‘good’ tableaux. These parallel encodings sharpen the proposed bijection problem.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Each within-model correspondence is asserted as straightforward; the source does not construct a bijection between the two tableau families F1 and F2.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Hankel paths realize the ASM-number determinant and yield a Catalan determinant proof
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The r=2 specialization defines P_n and proves it equals the critical binomial determinant. A related two-stage symmetric involution shows another central-binomial Hankel determinant counts 2^n right-angle path families, while the r=1 case gives a combinatorial proof that a Catalan Hankel determinant equals one.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: C=6 determinants have alternate binomial forms, while broader smoothness patterns appear to fail
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The five-term critical recurrence defines a moment functional whose first Hankel determinants match a higher-r binomial determinant row. Numerical factorization suggests the exceptional smooth product behavior at low orders does not persist for general binomial parameters a≥4.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Critical Hankel determinants equal the Robbins–Rumsey product by a computer-assisted triangularization, prior work equates that product with vertically symmetric ASMs, and this paper separately models the two sides by non-intersecting and osculating paths. A direct bijection between those path/tableau families would replace the product-mediated equality.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: No direct bijection is given, and the diagonal WZ certificate needed to audit the determinant evaluation is external to the source.
related_synthesis_entries.title: The ASM equality chain is proved algebraically but lacks the desired direct bijection
